options: Which rows of data a user can see, based on a DAX-filtered role they're assigned to
Which columns a user can see, regardless of row content
Which workspaces a user can open
Which Power BI license a user is allowed to purchase
questions.explain: RLS filters rows: a user assigned to a role only sees the rows that role's DAX expression evaluates to TRUE for. Restricting columns is a separate feature (OLS).

questions.q: What is the correct four-step RLS workflow, in order?
options: Define roles/rules in Desktop, publish, add members in the service, validate with Test as role
Add members, define roles, validate, then publish
Publish first, then define roles afterward in the service
Validate, publish, define roles, add members
questions.explain: Roles and DAX rules are defined in Desktop first, then published (bringing the role definitions along), then members are added to roles in the service, and finally validated with Test as role.

questions.q: Which workspace role does RLS actually restrict?
options: Only the Viewer role — Admins, Members, and Contributors have edit permission and RLS never applies to them
Only the Admin role
RLS applies equally to every workspace role
RLS only applies to users outside the workspace entirely
questions.explain: This is the detail most often missed: RLS restricts only Viewers. Anyone with Admin, Member, or Contributor access has edit permission on the semantic model, so RLS doesn't apply to them regardless of RLS role assignment.

questions.q: Can RLS be used to hide specific columns from a user while still showing them the row?
options: No — RLS only filters entire rows; hiding specific columns requires object-level security (OLS) instead
Yes, RLS and OLS are the same feature
Yes, but only for numeric columns
Only in DirectQuery mode
questions.explain: If a user can see a row at all through RLS, they see every column of it. Column/table-level restriction is a distinct feature called object-level security.

questions.q: If a user belongs to both a 'Sales' RLS role and a 'Marketing' RLS role, what do they see?
options: The union of both roles' data — everything either role's filter would show
Only the intersection — data both roles agree on
Neither role applies, and they see nothing
Whichever role was assigned first takes exclusive priority
questions.explain: RLS roles are additive. A user in multiple roles sees the combined (union) result of every role they belong to, not just the overlap between them.
